containers.title: Reporting grain — the peak of a range is the same number at every grain; only the buckets change

config.sqlTemplate: SELECT max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime)

SELECT round(sum(active_ms) / greatest(dateDiff('millisecond', greatest($__fromTime_ms, min(minute_start)), least($__toTime_ms, max(minute_start) + toIntervalMinute(1))), 1), 6) AS avg_concurrency FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime)
SELECT count() AS minutes_present FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime)

tiles.name: Benchmark answer set — exact peak and average per grouping, with the minute each peaked

config.sqlTemplate: SELECT multiIf(dim_mask=0,'(ungrouped)',dim_mask=1,'platform',dim_mask=2,'country',dim_mask=3,'platform + country',dim_mask=4,'content',dim_mask=5,'platform + content',dim_mask=8,'video_type',dim_mask=9,'platform + video_type',dim_mask=12,'content + video_type',dim_mask=15,'platform + country + content + video_type',dim_mask=16,'app_version',dim_mask=32,'category','full grain (all six)') AS grouping, dim_mask, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak, argMax(minute_start, minute_peak) AS peaked_at, round(sum(active_ms) / greatest(dateDiff('millisecond', greatest($__fromTime_ms, min(minute_start)), least($__toTime_ms, max(minute_start) + toIntervalMinute(1))), 1), 6) AS avg_concurrency, count() AS rows_read FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY dim_mask ORDER BY dim_mask

SELECT minute_start AS ts, minute_peak AS peak, round(active_ms / 60000.0, 3) AS time_weighted_average FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) ORDER BY ts

SELECT toStartOfHour(minute_start) AS ts, max(minute_peak) AS peak, round(sum(active_ms) / 3600000.0, 3) AS time_weighted_average FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts

SELECT toDate(minute_start) AS service_date, max(minute_peak) AS exact_peak, argMax(minute_start, minute_peak) AS peaked_at, round(sum(active_ms) / 86400000.0, 4) AS avg_over_full_day, round(sum(active_ms) / (count() * 60000.0), 3) AS avg_over_active_minutes, count() AS minutes_with_viewers FROM __DATABASE__.serving_minute_current WHERE dim_mask = 0 AND ($__timeFilter(minute_start) AND minute_start < $__toTime) GROUP BY service_date ORDER BY service_date

tiles.name: Pipeline evidence — what these answers actually read

config.sqlTemplate: SELECT any(query_id) AS sample_query_id, normalized_query_hash AS query_shape, count() AS runs, formatReadableQuantity(round(avg(read_rows))) AS avg_read_rows, formatReadableSize(round(avg(read_bytes))) AS avg_read_bytes, round(quantile(0.50)(query_duration_ms)) AS p50_ms, round(quantile(0.99)(query_duration_ms)) AS p99_ms, max(event_time) AS last_run FROM clusterAllReplicas(default, system.query_log) WHERE type = 'QueryFinish' AND $__timeFilter(event_time) AND positionCaseInsensitive(query, 'serving_minute_current') > 0 AND positionCaseInsensitive(query, 'system.query_log') = 0 GROUP BY query_shape ORDER BY avg(read_rows) DESC LIMIT 20

tiles.name: What this dashboard is, and how to read the answer set

config.markdown:
### The benchmark set, answered from the serving layer

The evaluation asks for **peak and average concurrency at minute, hour and day grain, with dimension filters**. Every number here comes from `serving_concurrency_minute` — a pre-aggregated table — not from re-deriving overlap out of the 905,558-row event history. The evidence tile at the bottom reports what each query actually read, because the brief is explicit that judges *"will look at what your queries read, not just how fast they return"*, and that **"no pipeline evidence, no credit"**.

### Peak is one number per range, not one per grain

The grain tabs change the reporting buckets, not the answer. From the brief: *"if minute 1 has 300K concurrent sessions, minute 2 has 200K, and minute 3 has 50K, the peak concurrency for the range (minutes 1–3) would be 300K."* Peak over a range is the maximum instantaneous value inside it, so the hourly peak is the max of that hour's minute peaks and the daily peak is the max of the day's — `max()` composes, which is why no separate hourly or daily table exists. The average does **not** compose that way and is always recomputed as `sum(active_ms) / duration`.

The day tab gives two averages on purpose. `avg_over_full_day` divides by a full 86,400s and is the honest per-day figure; `avg_over_active_minutes` divides only by minutes that had viewers, which is the right denominator when a day is sparse. On this extract Jul 15–20 hold no events at all, so the two differ by orders of magnitude and quoting the wrong one would flatter the numbers.

### Why the answer set has thirteen rows

Because a peak cannot be re-grouped after the fact. From the brief: *"a dimension like platform and a content might peak at one minute, while a combination like platform + country might reach its peak at an entirely different minute within the selected time range."* That is measurable here — over the hot hour the ungrouped peak lands at 10:55, content at 10:42, platform + content at 10:43, video_type at 10:56. So an exact peak is precomputed **at** each grouping (`dim_mask`) rather than derived at read time. Taking `max()` over a finer grain understates it: ANDROID_PHONE reads 1,461 from its own mask and 223 from the full-grain rows, a 6.5x error.

The thirteen are the ten `solution/policy.yaml` specifies (`0,1,2,4,8` and the combinations `3,5,9,12,15`) plus `16` app_version, `32` category and `63` full grain. `sum(active_ms)` is identical across all thirteen — that conservation check is what proves the fan-out neither drops nor duplicates a session. Groupings outside the list still get exact averages and exact instantaneous counts from mask 63, because `active_ms` and `ending_concurrency` are additive; only their peak degrades to an upper bound.

### Two things that will bite you reading these numbers

**`$__timeFilter` is inclusive at both ends.** A 10:00–11:00 selection returns 61 minutes, not 60. Every window here therefore carries an explicit `AND <col> < $__toTime` to make it half-open `[from, to)`, matching the interval convention the whole pipeline uses. Without it the average was 4.3% high — its numerator counted 61 minutes while its denominator capped at the selected span. The hot hour reads 2,305 and 855.603469 over 60 minutes; if the minute count ever shows 61, that guard has been dropped.

**ClickStack renders timestamps in the browser's timezone; this pipeline is UTC end to end.** On an IST machine the 10:55 UTC peak minute displays as 16:25, and a date picker set to "10:00–11:00" selects 04:30–05:30 UTC — which on this extract is a quiet period that reads a peak of 10 rather than 2,305. Set the range from UTC epochs (`?from=1785060000000&to=1785063600000` is the canonical hot hour) when the number has to be comparable to a reference figure.
